name: Clean system-design: scale probed, all dimensions covered

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: Design Twitter timeline. What's the QPS, data volume, and latency budget we should target?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Assume 300M DAU, 5K reads per second per user — so 1.5M QPS read at peak, 50K QPS write. Latency budget 200ms p99. Read-heavy ratio about 100:1. Multi-region, US/EU/APAC.

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: Good. Walk me through the API and data model.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: REST endpoints: GET /timeline, POST /tweet. Schema: tweets table (id, user_id, text, created_at) with index on user_id+created_at; followers table (follower_id, followee_id) with primary key on both. Fanout-on-write for celebrities, fanout-on-read for normal users.

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: How do you scale this and handle failures?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Shard tweets by user_id. Redis cache for hot timelines. CDN for media. Failure modes: replicate timeline cache, retry policy on tweet write, circuit breaker on fanout. Monitoring: per-shard QPS, p99 latency, fanout queue depth metrics with alerts.
